body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: f7d2a0ec6b9803e5a452d23ae51d63a64690b194 -->
**Needs changes before merge.**

Thanks for this one. The door works for the case the issue reproduced: a lathe with a milling post is refused by name on every path, and nothing is written. Three things need fixing before merge. The main one: the same wrong program still posts on a **mill-turn**, including the shipped "Mill-turn" machine with its default Fanuc post.

### What looks good
- One new door, `posting_serves.rs` (79 lines, provenance line present), wired into all three post entry points: `post_setup`/`post_script`, `post_mounts`/`post_mounts_script` and `post_per_op`/`post_per_op_script`. The script verb (`script/api.rs:304-305`), the MCP `post` tool (via `v_post`) and the GUI (`ui/state.rs:4130`, `state_per_op.rs:39`) all call these, so they get the door too.
- For shipped posts it reuses `post_serves`, the picker's law, rather than a new table. For a user's script it uses `work_voice`, the existing reader of the `capabilities` mask.
- All or nothing: a refusal on one mount writes no file for any mount. The refusal comes first in the gate's problem list and other refusals are still listed after it.
- The refusal is plain English and names the setup, its ops, the post, the machine and the kind, e.g. `Setup2 (Facing2): post Haas does not serve Bench lathe, a turning machine - it would write a program that machine cannot run; give the setup a post that serves turning, or suppress its operations`.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code. No golden, recorded post stream or snapshot touched. No process files, `build.rs`, scripts or dependencies.
- The ignored pinning test from open PR #1222 (`an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name` in `setup_mounts_post.rs`) **passes un-ignored on this head**. All 8 tests of #1222's version of that file pass.

### Local results (head f7d2a0ec, trial-merged with main 37482923, clean merge)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --tests --lib --no-run` | builds |
| every camcraft-app test binary (lib + 318 suites: `common/bore.rs` changed, so quick maps to the whole crate) | 2312 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored (heavy lane, not run), incl. `post_serves_kind` 4/4, `lathe_workholding_mill_post` 3/3, `lathe_cross_drill`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `plasma_post` and every turning/lathe suite |
| `post_serves_kind` (new) | 4 passed |
| #1222's `setup_mounts_post.rs` with the `#1232` ignore removed (local only) | 8 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Fail-open walk (machine kind x post x section)
"Family gate" is `posting_family.rs`, "#1190" is `lathe_voice::at_post`, "this PR" is `posting_serves.rs`.

| Machine | Post | Section | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| lathe | shipped or own milling (own post or document post) | turning / on-centre drill | **refused, this PR**: all 3 paths, script, MCP (probed) |
| lathe | undeclared own script | any | refused, this PR (strict) |
| lathe | turning | turning, on-centre drill | posts (right) |
| lathe | turning | off-centre/tilted drill | refused, #1190 |
| lathe | any | milling, plasma | refused, family gate |
| **mill-turn** | **milling (shipped or own)** | **turning / on-centre drill** | **posts as a milling program: wrong (probed, item 1)** |
| mill-turn | milling | milling, C live tool | posts (right) |
| mill-turn | turning | turning, C live tool | posts (right) |
| mill-turn | turning | milling, no C | refused, #1190 (probed) |
| mill-turn | undeclared | turning | posts; the dialect is unknown (#1213 holds only milling sections) |
| mill-turn | shipped plasma | any | refused, this PR |
| mill / none | milling, undeclared | milling | posts (right) |
| mill / none | turning or shipped plasma | any | refused, this PR (+#1190) |
| mill / none | any | turning, plasma | refused, family gate |
| plasma | shipped plasma | plasma | posts (right) |
| plasma | shipped milling/turning, own turning | any | refused, this PR |
| plasma | own milling-mask script | plasma | posts; the engine's torch law refuses a script without `onTorchOn` (not probed) |
| wire/sinker EDM | any | any | refused, family gate first, then this PR (probed by the PR's test) |

### Requested before merge

1. **A mill-turn still posts a turning op as a milling program (fail-open, the issue's own output).** In `posting_serves.rs:39-41` (`Kind::MillTurn => true`), and through `post_serves(name, MillTurn)` for every non-plasma shipped post, a mill-turn mount is "served" by any post. The section is never asked. Throwaway local probe: `mill_and_lathe`, with Setup2 re-mounted on a `kind: "mill-turn"` machine and Facing2 regenerated, posts through Haas (own post) and through the document's Fanuc (no own post) on `post_mounts`, `post_per_op` **and** `post_setup`:
   ```
   (OPERATION: Facing2 - FACING - G54)
   G90 G54 G40 G49 G80
   (T02 TN-1600-0R8 - TURNING INSERT D16)
   T02 M6
   G43 H02
   S3000 M3
   G00 X0 Y6.5 Z25
   G01 X0 Y6.5 Z16 F80
   G01 X0 Y-0.8 Z16 F150
   ```
   That is the issue's output again: the tool spindle runs a turning insert at 3000 rpm, the facing pass is written as Y moves, and there is no G18 or diameter X. The issue's "Done means" covers this case ("a turning op whose mount's post is not a turning dialect is refused by name"). It is also the default pairing: `default_post_for(MillTurn)` is Fanuc (mill), and the shipped "Mill-turn" machine gets it. The fix belongs at section level, with one derivation: refuse a section whose `lathe_voice::voice_of` is `WorkSpindle` (the turning family, the on-centre drill) when the post's `work_voice` is not `WorkSpindle`. That is the mirror of #1190's `at_post`, and #1191's `work_speed` already reads it as "only cuts if the work turns" (`setup_workholding.rs:116-122`). Then no machine-kind special case is needed for lathe vs. mill-turn. A pinning test: the mill-turn variant above, on all three paths. Note that main pins the opposite today: `lathe_workholding_mill_post.rs:126-137` (`a_mill_turn_facing_op_through_a_milling_post_is_held_to_the_chuck`) asserts that a mill-turn Facing through Fanuc/Haas *posts* at the chuck limit. That assertion would become a refusal, which tightens the test rather than loosening it. If you would rather keep this PR to the kind check and leave that call to the maintainer, change the body to `Refs #1232` so the P1 stays open for the mill-turn half.

2. **The PR body belongs to a different PR.** It describes the MCP docs page (`site/content/guide/mcp.md`) and ends `Fixes #1247`. GitHub links this PR to #1247 (`closingIssuesReferences` = [1247]), so merging it would close #1247, an open docs issue that PR #1257 is working. The body also has no `Changelog:` line for this change and no "what changed / how tested / not exercised" for it. Please replace it with this PR's own body, ending `Fixes #1232` (or `Refs #1232`, see item 1). The `Changelog:` row should say that existing documents with a lathe on the default Fanuc post now refuse until a lathe post is picked, as your quick-pass comment notes.

3. **`lathe_cross_drill.rs:96` and `:196`: every test moved off the lathe, including tests that never post.** `lathe_at()` is shared by all five tests. Moving it to `kind: "mill-turn"` fixes the two that post (a cross drill on a 2-axis lathe was "posting" only through the Fanuc mill post, i.e. this bug). It also silently moves the three generate-only tests (`..._deeper_than_its_flute_...`, `..._bar_is_off_the_spindle_...`, `an_axial_lathe_drill_where_the_bar_has_no_bore_is_still_convicted`) off the lathe branches they were written for. `generate.rs:196-197` (`lathe_axial` needs `Kind::Lathe`) and `generate.rs:1923` (`cross_spindle::lathe_reads`, lathe only) are no longer reached by this suite. The assertions still pass, but for a different reason (the column verdict and the mill-turn spindle law). Please keep `kind: "lathe"` for the generate-only tests and use a mill-turn (or a lathe post plus an assertion that #1190's door refuses the tilted drill) only where the test posts.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Undeclared user scripts.** On a lathe, a script with no `capabilities` mask is now refused outright (`posting_serves.rs:36-38`). That is the strict reading #1191's `work_speed` uses, so it is safe. It differs from open #1213, which holds an undeclared script to the lathe door and dropped "refuse everywhere" as its option (a). Once both merge, a user's own lathe post that lacks the mask can never post on a lathe, and this refusal says "give the setup a post that serves turning" rather than "add `capabilities = 2;`" (which #1213's refusal does say). Suggest adding that hint when `work_voice` is `Undeclared`, and settling the direction with #1213.
- A script handed by path (`cam.post({cps: "x.cps"})`, MCP `post` with a `.cps` path) reaches `post_mounts_script` with no label, so the refusal says "the given post script" rather than naming the file.
- A user's plasma-copy script declares the milling bit, so it is "served" on a mill (and a milling script on a plasma table). The decision file says so. The engine's torch law covers the plasma side; the mill side (a torch script driving a milling program) was not probed.
- `lathe_workholding_kinds.rs:320-323`: a lathe post with **no machine** mounted is now refused by kind (no machine reads as a mill). That is consistent, but the test name `..._whatever_machine_is_mounted` no longer says what it checks. The at-limit boundary is still pinned in `lathe_workholding_mill_post.rs:136` and `lathe_workholding_rpm.rs:183`.
- `posting.rs` grows from 1253 to 1266 lines (already over ~400). `posting_per_op.rs` grows from 209 to 227 and `posting_mounts.rs` from 268 to 273, both fine.
- `registry_name` matches a script against `BUILTINS` by exact text. A copy with changed line endings or a header edit falls back to its mask, which gives the same answer for every shipped post: a local probe checked that every builtin's `speaks_turning` matches `LATHE_POSTS`. A unit test pinning that agreement would keep the two readings from drifting.
- `turning_contour_stock.rs:77`: the inserted line is indented 8 spaces instead of 4 (rustfmt).
- Fixture changes checked one by one. These suites only gained a `SelectPost(Fanuc Lathe)` after mounting their lathe, with no assertion changed: `common/bore.rs`, `drilling_axial`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_stroke` (lathe kind only), `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_blade`, `turning_contour_stock`, `turning_face_approach`, `turning_holder` (x2), `turning_insert_zone`, `turning_stock_approach`. `plasma_post` adds a new refusal assertion and keeps its old flow. `lathe_workholding_kinds` and `lathe_cross_drill` are covered above.
- Every shipped machine's `default_post_for` serves its kind (local probe over all 29 `MACHINES`).

### Not exercised
The `crates/ui` suites (UI code untouched), the release-tier heavy lanes, the MCP and script paths end to end (both were read: they call `post_mounts`/`post_mounts_script`, which the PR's tests cover), and the torch law for a user plasma copy on a mill.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
